name: Nike
clues: They design gear that helps people run, jump, and play sports.
Founded in the 1960s; headquartered in the Pacific Northwest of the United States.
They're famous for sneakers worn by some of the world's greatest athletes.
They started out selling shoes from the trunk of a car at track meets.

name: Starbucks
clues: They sell drinks many grown-ups say they can't start the morning without.
Founded in the 1970s; headquartered in Seattle.
They're famous for handing you a warm cup with your name written on it.
They began as a single store selling roasted beans near a famous fish market.

name: Disney
clues: They tell stories that kids and families around the world grow up with.
Founded in the 1920s; headquartered in Southern California.
They run theme parks where you can meet your favorite characters in person.
The whole company was built on a cartoon mouse the founder first sketched on a train ride.

name: McDonald's
clues: They serve quick meals to millions of people every single day.
Became a franchise business in the 1950s; headquartered in Chicago.
They're famous for burgers, fries, and golden arches you can spot from the highway.
They make much of their money as a landlord — collecting rent from the people who run their restaurants.

name: Tesla
clues: They build machines that get people from place to place without using gasoline.
Founded in the 2000s; headquartered in Texas.
They're famous for electric cars that update themselves overnight, like a phone.
They also make giant batteries that can power an entire house when the lights go out.

name: Visa
clues: Their product fits in a wallet, but their real business is invisible.
Founded in the 1950s; headquartered in Northern California.
They're famous for the network that moves money when you tap or swipe at a checkout.
They don't lend anyone money — they take a tiny slice of trillions of dollars of payments every year.

name: Roblox
clues: They make a place where kids don't just play games — they build them.
Founded in the 2000s; headquartered in Northern California.
Their most famous product lets you build entire worlds out of virtual blocks with friends.
Most of the experiences on their platform were created by kids and teenagers, not company employees.

name: Spotify
clues: They deliver something you can't see or touch, but probably hear every day.
Founded in the 2000s; headquartered in Sweden.
They're famous for playlists that learn exactly what you like.
They were started to fight music piracy — by making listening easier than stealing.

name: Ford
clues: They've been building the machines families ride in for over a century.
Founded in the 1900s; headquartered in Michigan.
They're famous for pickup trucks that have been America's best-selling vehicles for decades.
Their founder perfected the moving assembly line, cutting the time to build a car from half a day to about 90 minutes.

name: Verizon
clues: They run an invisible network you probably used in the last five minutes.
Formed in the 2000s from older phone companies; headquartered in New York.
They're famous for the wireless service that keeps phones connected coast to coast.
Their name was invented by gluing a Latin word for truth onto a word for the edge of the sky.

name: Costco
clues: You can't shop there unless your family pays to be a member.
Founded in the 1980s; headquartered near Seattle.
They're famous for selling everything in giant sizes — and a famously cheap hot-dog combo.
They make almost all their profit from membership fees, not from the stuff on the shelves.

name: Netflix
clues: They changed how families spend their evenings at home.
Founded in the 1990s; headquartered in Northern California.
They're famous for shows you can watch the moment they come out — a whole season at once.
They started by mailing discs in red envelopes, and once offered to sell themselves to a video-rental chain that said no.
